paragraphs.text: Oocyte/zygote/embryo maturation arrest-29 (OZEMA29) is a form of female infertility. Reported features include oocyte maturation arrest and degeneration, impaired ovarian folliculogenesis, diminished ovarian reserve, failure of superovulation, and repeated failure of in vitro fertilization (IVF) (He et al., 2020; Yang et al., 2021; Wang et al., 2021; Du et al., 2023). Ruotsalainen et al. (2024) noted that all affected individuals published up to that time had primary infertility that did not respond to treatment.

checks.evidence_quote: A recurrent mutation in TBPL2 causes diminished ovarian reserve and female infertility.

paragraphs.text: Ruotsalainen et al. (2024) studied women in the Finnish FinnGen cohort who were homozygous for a TBPL2 stop-gained variant (R299X). These women had significantly fewer offspring than women in the other genotype groups: an average of 0.16 (SD = 0.58) offspring, compared with an average of 1.75 (p = 1.4 x 10(-15)). Of the 41 homozygous women, 2 had given birth to 1 child and 2 had given birth to more than 1 child. All 4 of these women had undergone IVF therapy, but no information was available on whether donor oocytes had been used. In phenome-wide association analysis, the variant was associated only with infertility and with no other diseases.

paragraphs.text: Yang et al. (2021) performed whole-exome sequencing in 2 unrelated infertile families with oocyte maturation defects and confirmed the findings by Sanger sequencing. Affected women in both families were homozygous for a splice site mutation in the TBPL2 gene (c.788+3A-G). Haplotype analysis indicated that the disease alleles in the 2 families had arisen independently. In a minigene assay, the variant disrupted the integrity of TBPL2 mRNA. Transcriptome sequencing of affected oocytes showed that genes vital for oocyte maturation and fertilization were broadly and markedly downregulated. The authors noted that direct functional evidence was lacking.

paragraphs.text: Du et al. (2023) performed whole-exome sequencing in a 32-year-old woman with primary infertility and impaired ovarian folliculogenesis. They identified compound heterozygous mutations in the TBPL2 gene: a novel c.802C-T transition resulting in an arg268-to-ter (R268X) substitution, and the previously reported c.788+3A-G variant, which they designated p.Arg233Ter. The mutations were confirmed by Sanger sequencing in the patient and her family members. Allele frequencies were checked in the ExAC and gnomAD databases, and the variants were predicted to be deleterious by SIFT, MutationTaster, and CADD.

paragraphs.text: Ruotsalainen et al. (2024) performed a genome-wide association study in the Finnish FinnGen cohort of 22,849 women with infertility and 198,989 control women who had given birth. The recessive analysis identified a stop-gained variant in the TBPL2 gene (c.895A-T, NM_199047.3), resulting in an arg299-to-ter (R299X) substitution. The variant was associated with infertility with an odds ratio of 650.1 (p = 4.11 x 10(-25)), an effect comparable to highly penetrant monogenic mutations. Women homozygous for the variant had significantly fewer offspring than other women. The premature stop codon lies in the DNA-binding part of the protein, and the variant was predicted to be a high-confidence loss-of-function variant with a CADD score of 40.

checks.claim: The odds ratio for infertility with TBPL2 R299X was 650.1 (p = 4.11 x 10(-25)).
checks.evidence_quote: at the TBPL2 locus on chromosome 14 with an odds ratio (OR) of 650.1 (p = 4.11 × 10−25).

checks.claim: The TBPL2 R299X variant had a minor allele frequency of 1.1% in Finland.
checks.evidence_quote: minor-allele frequency [MAF]: 1.1% in Finland

checks.claim: The TBPL2 R299X variant was enriched 43-fold in Finland relative to non-Finnish Europeans.
checks.evidence_quote: that is highly enriched to Finland (43 times compared to non-Finnish Europeans).

checks.claim: Women homozygous for TBPL2 R299X had an average of 0.16 offspring.
checks.evidence_quote: with women carrying two copies of the risk allele having an average of only 0.16 (SD = 0.58) offspring.

checks.claim: Of the 41 women homozygous for TBPL2 R299X, only 4 had given birth.
checks.evidence_quote: According to the registry data, only four homozygous women for the TBPL2 mutation had children, and all of them had received infertility treatment
checks.explanation: Four homozygous women had children. The total of 41 homozygous women is given in the Discussion.

checks.claim: All 4 women homozygous for TBPL2 R299X who had given birth had undergone IVF.
checks.evidence_quote: All four women had undergone IVF therapy, although more detailed information on the potential use of donor oocytes is not available.
